slides.texte_overlay:
hobbies that will make you
disgustingly intelligent

prediction journal

every sunday, write down 3 predictions about anything, news, work, friends, and check them a month later. being wrong on paper is the fastest way to start thinking clearly.

the three source rule

before you believe something you read online, find it in 3 different places. it takes 2 minutes, and it slowly turns you into the person nobody can fool.

morning chess puzzles

solve 3 chess puzzles every morning instead of checking your phone. it trains you to see a few moves ahead, which is exactly what smart people do everywhere else.

morning lessons

every morning, give 5 minutes to one short lesson on something new: a battle, a planet, a philosopher. small daily doses add up to the kind of knowledge people assume took years.

morning lessons

every morning, give 5 minutes to one short lesson on something new: a battle, a planet, a philosopher. a micro-learning app like the Sophia app makes it easy, and it adds up faster than you think.

slides.texte_overlay:
one sentence summaries

after every video or article, sum it up in one sentence before you move on. it feels slow at first, then it becomes the reason you actually remember what you learn.
